beforeRecord.q: An economy has a recessionary gap after aggregate demand falls. While wages are adjusting downward, a permanent productivity improvement raises productive capacity. Which conclusion best separates the two long-run forces?
options: The productivity gain shifts aggregate demand right while wage adjustment shifts LRAS left, so both forces alter potential output in opposite directions.
The original demand shock permanently fixes real output below potential, so neither wage adjustment nor improved productivity can change the long-run outcome.
SRAS adjustment helps close the demand-created gap, while higher productivity can shift LRAS right and change the potential-output target.
Both changes should be treated as the same SRAS movement, because productive capacity does not affect the location of LRAS in this model.
beforeRecord.commonError: Assumes every fall in real GDP is a temporary gap around an unchanged potential-output level.
beforeRecord.feedback: Before forecasting self-correction back to the old output level, check whether productive capacity changed and LRAS shifted.

afterRecord.q: A fall in aggregate demand creates a recessionary gap. As wages fall, a permanent productivity improvement also raises the economy’s productive capacity. How does each change affect the economy’s long-run adjustment?
options: The productivity gain shifts aggregate demand right while wage adjustment shifts LRAS left, so both forces alter potential output in opposite directions.
The original demand shock permanently fixes real output below potential, so neither wage adjustment nor improved productivity can change the long-run outcome.
SRAS adjustment helps close the demand-created gap, while higher productivity can shift LRAS right and change the potential-output target.
Both changes should be treated as the same SRAS movement, because productive capacity does not affect the location of LRAS in this model.
afterRecord.commonError: Assumes every fall in real GDP is a temporary gap around an unchanged potential-output level.
afterRecord.feedback: Falling wages shift short-run aggregate supply right and help close the original recessionary gap. Higher productivity also shifts long-run aggregate supply right, raising potential output. The economy therefore adjusts toward a new potential output rather than simply returning to the old level.

beforeRecord.q: With nominal money supply fixed, the price level and borrowing rate both rise. Firms also become more optimistic, shifting desired investment outward at every rate, and observed investment rises. Other influences are unchanged. Which account fits the evidence, and what would investment have done had the price level stayed fixed?
options: The rate channel restrains investment but optimism outweighs it; with the price level fixed, investment would rise even more
The rate channel raises investment and optimism restrains it; with the price level fixed, investment would rise even more
The rate channel restrains investment and optimism is irrelevant; with the price level fixed, investment would fall
The rate channel raises investment and optimism reinforces it; with the price level fixed, investment would remain unchanged
beforeRecord.commonError: Attributes rising observed investment to the price-level channel when a separate investment shift outweighs its restraint.
beforeRecord.feedback: At fixed nominal money supply, a higher price level raises money demand and the borrowing rate, restraining investment along its schedule. The separate optimistic shift raises investment enough to offset that restraint. Removing the price-level increase removes the restraint, so investment would rise more. A movement along AD is distinct from an independent spending shift.

The rate channel raises investment and optimism restrains it; with the price level fixed, investment would rise even more
The rate channel restrains investment and optimism is irrelevant; with the price level fixed, investment would fall
The rate channel raises investment and optimism reinforces it; with the price level fixed, investment would remain unchanged
afterRecord.commonError: Attributes rising observed investment to the price-level channel when a separate investment shift outweighs its restraint.
afterRecord.feedback: With a fixed nominal money supply, a higher price level raises interest rates and discourages investment. Greater business optimism more than offsets that effect. Without the price-level increase, investment would rise even further.
